program.identity: Environmental Science Labs District — The Living Transect
program.architecturalLanguage: buildings as enlarged scientific instruments operating across ocean, atmosphere, water, soil, ecosystems, contaminants, carbon, climate adaptation, robotics, and planetary modelling

buildings.name: Tellus Earth Systems Convergence
buildings.subtitle: Planetary Modelling and Integrated Observation
buildings.focus: Planetary modelling, environmental digital twins, and integrated Earth observation
buildings.exteriorSignature: three incomplete elliptical contour rings around a geological world court and instrumented skeletal globe

buildings.name: Aeolian Atmospheric Observatory
buildings.subtitle: Atmospheric Chemistry and Cloud Physics
buildings.focus: Greenhouse gases, aerosols, cloud microphysics, and marine-atmosphere sampling
buildings.exteriorSignature: rounded three-bladed atmospheric tower with five instrument halos, aerostat apron, and calibration mast forest

buildings.name: Hydrological Extremes Institute
buildings.subtitle: Flood, Drought and Groundwater Systems
buildings.focus: Floods, droughts, groundwater, isotope hydrology, and watershed prediction
buildings.exteriorSignature: seven descending watershed terraces cut by an artificial ravine, exposed flumes, and a floodable plaza

buildings.name: Littoral Exchange Laboratory
buildings.subtitle: Ocean-Land Interface Research
buildings.focus: Coastal dynamics, ocean acidification, marine ecology, and land-sea exchange
buildings.exteriorSignature: segmented semi-submerged shoreline crescent, tidal basins, habitat breakwater, research pier, and Exchange Disc

buildings.name: Biotic Continuum Observatory
buildings.subtitle: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Monitoring
buildings.focus: Biodiversity genomics, environmental DNA, acoustic ecology, and species migration
buildings.exteriorSignature: branching elevated phylogenetic structure, habitat corridors, dome bridges, ecological roof strips, and Biodiversity Mast

buildings.name: Critical Zone and Rhizosphere Institute
buildings.subtitle: Soil, Roots and Subsurface Ecosystems
buildings.focus: Soil systems, root ecology, weathering, nutrient cycles, and subsurface microbiology
buildings.exteriorSignature: partially buried geological terraces, exposed soil-profile court, core towers, boreholes, and instrumented root columns

buildings.name: Carbon Transformation Foundry
buildings.subtitle: Carbon Removal and Biogeochemical Engineering
buildings.focus: Direct air capture, mineralization, enhanced weathering, and carbon-cycle engineering
buildings.exteriorSignature: dark mineralized laboratory, six modular capture towers, three mineral silos, exposed pipes, and weathering yard

buildings.name: Anthropocene Forensics Centre
buildings.subtitle: Emerging Pollutant Source Attribution
buildings.focus: PFAS, microplastics, nanoplastics, environmental exposomics, and source attribution
buildings.exteriorSignature: sealed recycled-glass black monolith split by five pathway fissures and crowned by a dense sampler field

buildings.name: Climate Resilience Proving House
buildings.subtitle: Adaptation Systems Test Complex
buildings.focus: Flood, heat, drought, wildfire, storm, and infrastructure-failure adaptation
buildings.exteriorSignature: reinforced test spine with twelve replaceable facade bays, travelling storm frame, flood plaza, and Heat Canyon

buildings.name: Gaia Field Systems Fleetworks
buildings.subtitle: Autonomous Observation and Ecosystem Repair
buildings.focus: Environmental drones, autonomous boats, field robots, sensing networks, and ecosystem restoration
buildings.exteriorSignature: low boomerang robotic hangar around a launch court, operational roof, calibration facade, canal door, and communications mast
